owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. ONE BOUND IS NOT CC's TO MOVE and it is the obvious wrong fix: the repair may NOT be to forbid a journal from opening mid-path. Four of the six component journals in the corpus open past BUILDME and all four are legitimate — they are pre-gate components (2026-07-27) whose voyages were already underway when the workflow system arrived, and a rule that reds them retroactively is a rule that reds history for being old.
intention: The two gates that guard BUILDME — `buildme_rides_the_chart` and `buildme_rides_the_intent` — hold jurisdiction over a build that HAPPENED, not only over the act of crossing into it, so a voyage cannot skip them by opening its journal with the cursor already past BUILDME.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, twice: once against the live corpus, once by running the gate both ways over the same input.

THE GATE'S JURISDICTION IS A CROSSING. `transitions.py:1423` reads `if target == "BUILDME" and target_idx > wf.cursor:` — the entry gate fires when, and only when, the move being journaled lands ON BUILDME. Its siblings sit the same way: the build gate keys off `wf.here == "PROVEME"`, the exit gate off `target == "PROVED"`. For every other gate that is exactly right, because the thing each guards IS a crossing. For the entry gate it is not, because the thing it guards is that A BUILD WAS CHARTED — and a build is a period, not an edge.

THE A/B THAT PROVES IT. One cast ticket with no berthed chart chain (`constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured`), two emits, scratch history paths:

  A. `[TICKETME] -> BUILDME`   REFUSED EntryGateRed — 'no berthed chart chain claims ticket ... the build has no charted course'. Nothing journaled.
  B. `[BUILDME] -> PROVEME`    PASSED. Three checks proved — the_target_is_in_the_vocabulary, the_crossing_moves_the_cursor, the_crossing_is_a_legal_edge. `entry_gate` field: null.

Same ticket. Same missing chain. The difference is entirely which edge the journal opened on, and the second route is one keystroke of the workflow string away from the first.

AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS WALKED TODAY. `cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/history.json` seq 0, at 2026-08-14, is `THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME:waiting] -> ...`, ticket `orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured`, three checks proved, `entry_gate: null`. That ticket has NO berthed chart chain (grep over every packet in `~/.cairn/devices/chart/` for its id returns nothing) and NO intent berth (`intent_berth: None`) — and it stands at PROVED. Both BUILDME gates were owed and neither was paid, and the record of the voyage is clean because nothing ever asked.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a reader looking at orient's history sees a complete, well-formed voyage with every check it was asked for passing. The absence is invisible at the surface where it matters, because a gate that never ran leaves no trace of not running — the `entry_gate` field is null for 'exempt', null for 'not applicable', and null for 'never asked'. That is the same class of failure as the 2026-07-24 'done' reported while the files stood unmoved: not a lie, a question nobody put.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. The chart requirement IS physics on one edge and policy everywhere else on the same path, which means it is policy.
Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. A build whose preamble was never run is the hollow shape the chain exists to refuse, and it reached PROVED.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. That the gate covered BUILDME was assumed for as long as it has existed; two emits said otherwise.
Akien 2026-08-14 — 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid'. This is the workflow's own floor with a door in it.

the_census_behind_the_scope.of_those_pre_gate: 4 — build_inspector, tools/orient, intention_extractor, librarian, all 2026-07-27, all with ZERO checks recorded. The gate landed 2026-07-29 (ticket a-voyage-names-its-ticket). These are not misuse; they are components whose journals began before the physics existed, and the fix must leave them alone.
the_census_behind_the_scope.of_those_post_gate: 1 — builder/machines/orient, 2026-08-14, three checks, live gate, real cast ticket, no chain. This is the whole finding.
the_census_behind_the_scope.so: One walk, today, is the honest count. It is not a corpus-wide pattern and this ticket does not claim one. It matters because of WHEN: the same session was about to take the same route for constrain, and the reason it did not is that the ticket sat at TICKETME so route A was the only one available. The next build whose ticket happens to sit one state further along meets no gate at all.

gates: (1) THE PREDICATE IS ABOUT THE BUILD, NOT THE EDGE. Whatever ships must be able to answer 'was this component's build charted?' at a crossing that is not the BUILDME edge — the natural place is the same crossing the build gate already owns (leaving PROVEME), because that is the first moment the system is told a build finished. (2) A JOURNAL MAY STILL OPEN MID-PATH. See the owner clause: four legitimate cases exist and a fix that reds them has traded one false reading for four. The distinction the repair must draw is pre-gate-component vs skipped-gate, and it is drawable — the four carry zero checks and predate the gate's ticket. (3) NULL MUST STOP MEANING THREE THINGS. `entry_gate: null` currently reads as exempt, not-applicable, and never-asked. A record of truth that cannot distinguish 'this gate passed you' from 'this gate never saw you' is Law 7's collapse at a diagnostic surface. (4) NO RETROACTIVE JUDGEMENT OF SEALED VOYAGES without Akien's ruling — see `the_question_that_rides_along`.
falsifier: DONE when the A/B above is re-run and route B refuses for the same reason route A does, AND the four pre-gate journals still stand unred under a full shake, AND `entry_gate` distinguishes never-asked from passed in the record. WRONG INTENT if: (1) a journal is forbidden from opening mid-path — that reds four legitimate histories to close one hole; (2) the gate is moved to fire on EVERY crossing, which asks a chart of a back-edge retreat and makes a kick-back impossible, the motion a red exists to produce; (3) orient's sealed PROVED is quietly re-opened or its record edited — history is append-only (Law 7) and what is owed there is a new record, not a corrected old one; (4) the fix ships and nothing measures it, given that the only reason this was found is that a build happened to be standing at the other edge.
horizon: Small and it is one predicate moved, plus the null-collapse in the journal field. The part that is NOT one build is what to do about the voyage that already walked through — that is the question below, and it is Akien's.

the_question_that_rides_along.question: orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured is PROVED, sealed, and its build was never charted. Does it owe its chain retroactively, or does it stand?
the_question_that_rides_along.why_it_is_yours_and_not_CC's: Both answers are defensible and they build different things. CC will not pick by which one costs less work — that is the disposition the 2026-08-14 rule forbids wearing a design argument's clothes.
the_question_that_rides_along.reading_it_stands: The gate did not ask, so nothing was smuggled past a question that was put. The build is real, its proofs are real, its watch is armed and its validation is sealed; what is missing is the preamble's LEARNING (the trees got no deposit), not the build's correctness. Cost of this reading: a voyage that skipped the preamble is indistinguishable at rest from one that ran it, forever.
the_question_that_rides_along.reading_it_owes: The chain is what authorizes a build, and an unauthorized build in proven-space is exactly Law 8's hollow. Cost of this reading, stated plainly so it is not chosen by accident: the only way to pay it is to author orient/survey/decompose KNOWING the answers, which produces a chain that is true about content and fiction about sequence — and once that is done for one voyage it is available to every future one as 'chart it afterwards'. That is the gate learning to accept its own bypass.
the_question_that_rides_along.what_CC_did_with_the_sibling_while_this_: Nothing that presumes either answer. `constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured` is in the identical position (code committed at fe71a6d, 16 proof teeth, validation sealed, WATCHME probe armed, ticket at TICKETME, no chain, no component history at all) and CC did NOT take route B to move it, and did NOT author it a retroactive chart. It stays where it is with the finding recorded on it.

dependencies: Reads on the standing trouble `workflow-cursor-unreadable-by-the-chokepoint` only to say this is NOT that. That trouble is about ticket state strings the chokepoint cannot parse; this is about a chokepoint that parses the string perfectly and asks the wrong question of it. Related measurement, different defect.

SIBLING HALF, ALREADY MEASURED AND NOT RE-DERIVED HERE: `constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured` distinction 47 measured the TICKET-FILE side of the same skip — across the 41 tickets ever cast through /sorted, orient's is the only one carrying no intent_berth, and git shows its file was first committed with the cursor already at [BUILDME], a position no crossing ever moved it to, because /sorted refuses a cast cursor past TICKETME and the ticket FILE has no door at all (the casting-has-no-chokepoint IOU in cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py). THE TWO HALVES COMPOUND AND EITHER ALONE WOULD HAVE HELD: an honestly-cast ticket at TICKETME still meets no entry gate if the JOURNAL opens past BUILDME, which is this ticket, and a correctly-jurisdictioned gate still never fires if the ticket file was born past it, which is that one. Fixing one leaves the other open.
distinctions_recorded: A GATE THAT NEVER RAN AND A GATE THAT PASSED YOU LEAVE THE SAME RECORD. `entry_gate: null` covers both, plus 'exempt'. This is the part that makes the hole invisible rather than merely present, and it is separately fixable from the jurisdiction itself — worth noting because the jurisdiction fix alone would leave every past record still unreadable.

FOUR LEGITIMATE MID-PATH OPENINGS AND ONE SKIP LOOK IDENTICAL TO A GREP. The shape 'journal opens past BUILDME' is not the defect; it is the defect's silhouette. What separates them is the gate's existence at the time, which is a date comparison against a ticket — cheap, but it has to be drawn or the fix reds history.

THE HOLE WAS FOUND BY A BUILD STANDING AT THE OTHER EDGE. constrain's ticket sat at TICKETME, so the only crossing available was the guarded one, and it refused. Had that ticket sat one state further along — as its sibling's did — the same build would have sailed clean and nothing would have been found. The instrument here was luck, and that is the argument for gate (4)'s standing measurement.

THE TICKET ABOUT THE BUILDME GATES COULD NOT ITSELF CROSS BUILDME — and not for its own reason. Cast by hand 2026-08-14, it carried a bare WATCHME (a summons naming no object) and `sorted_berth: null`, so `buildme_rides_the_sorted` would have refused it at the very edge it is about, for a different missing field. Re-fired through /sorted 2026-08-17 (berth sorted-20260817T225912-eef4f0a63ede.json). The population, measured: all four hand casts of 2026-08-14 carry both gaps, because each was written by copying a sibling — which is how a missing field propagates rather than recurring.

THIS TICKET BUYS DETECTION WHERE THE BUILDME EDGE BUYS PREVENTION, and naming the difference is what stops a later reader from mistaking it for a claim that the hole is closed. Asking 'was this build charted?' at the PROVEME exit is the right EVENT — it is the first moment the system is told a build finished — and it is strictly later than the harm. The earlier alternative, forbidding a journal from opening mid-path, is a named WRONG INTENT because it reds four legitimate pre-gate histories to close one hole. So the trade is deliberate, not an oversight.
provenance: Found 2026-08-14 while dispositioning the EntryGateRed that refused constrain's BUILDME crossing. The refusal was correct; asking why its sibling had not met the same refusal is what surfaced this. The A/B probe was run into scratch history paths and discarded; nothing was journaled at any real component address by this investigation.
intent_berth: none, because this is a bug: the gate's jurisdiction is one predicate in one `if` at transitions.py:1423 and editing lines of code fixes it (ruling 2026-08-02, three entry points). No new intention is being born — `buildme_rides_the_chart` already intends that a build rides a chart, and this is the code failing to mean it everywhere the build is.

watchme.trigger: every PROVED crossing through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit — the chokepoint is the sole path, so the crossing IS the event and nothing polls; the probe asks of the component that just crossed whether its build was charted, by the same predicate the fix installs
watchme.enough: when twenty PROVED crossings have each carried a charted build AND at least one crossing has been REFUSED by the moved predicate — the refusal is the half that matters, because a gate that has never refused anything is indistinguishable from a gate that cannot. Stop early and loudly on the first PROVED crossing whose build was never charted and which the predicate let through: that is the hole reopening, and it is a finding rather than a sample
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: per crossing, whether a validate berth claims the ticket, where the journal opened, whether the component is pre-gate by the date test, and what entry_gate records — never-asked, passed, or exempt, now told apart
watchme.nexus: the workflow chokepoint's own diagnostic trail, because the question is about this seam's jurisdiction and the consumer is whoever is deciding whether a crossing may be trusted
watchme.consumer: harbor_master.clearance, which leans on PROVED being earned, and Akien at his gate for the one question this ticket does not decide — what is owed by the voyage that already walked through
